newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb blast damages French post office.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast damages French post office.

text.p: A bomb exploded outside the post office in the southern French town of Aix-en-Provence early on Monday, a few hours before a Franco-Spanish summit was to open in nearby Marseille.

Police said the blast badly damaged the building but caused no injuries. No one has claimed responsibility for the blast. Corsican separatists bombed the law courts in Aix-en-Provence a few weeks ago.

French President Jacques Chirac and Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maris Aznar, accompanied by their top cabinet ministers, were due to begin a two-day meeting later in the day in Marseille, 30 km (18 miles) south of Aix-en-Provence.
Spain, and France to a lesser degree, face a violent campaign by Basque separatists.

On the French Mediterranean island of Corsica, a bomb blast early on Monday destroyed a private car belonging to conservative Senator Louis-Ferdinand de Rocca Serra in the village of Levie where he is mayor. No one was injured. Another bomb planted under his official car was defused.
The attacks appeared to be part of a bombing campaign by the hardline separatist "Historic Wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) against elected officials on the island.
